task_specification.objective: Restore a closure-ready ordinary Mournlight release path: make fresh input traverse all five waves and defeat Bellkeeper once, preserve an authored readable arena and truthful upgrade choices, guarantee clean Result/Retry lifecycle, and leave dense profiling ready for native three-cycle host qualification without fabricating renderer evidence.

diagnosis.root_cause: The authoritative wave director has accumulated extensive diagnostic and receipt logic, but the latest ordinary replay still remained in Wave 1 and never exercised the contiguous five-wave-to-Bellkeeper path; the stable Wave 4 fixture cannot qualify ordinary progression. The dense contract is structurally present but native qualification is blocked by an external llvmpipe renderer and unavailable candidate-bound MCP collection. Release qualification therefore needs direct-owner route repair, player-facing release-shell and spatial validation, and host-ready dense receipts rather than more transform tuning or synthetic fixtures.

stop_conditions: Stop route work when fresh ordinary input still cannot advance contiguously beyond Wave 1 after one direct wave-owner pass; record the exact transition and preserve the diagnostic fixture as non-qualifying.

Stop dense implementation when receipts are candidate-complete but the host remains on software rendering; carry native qualification as external evidence debt rather than changing the renderer gate or inventing samples.
Stop visual changes if the intact authored cemetery package would require destructive asset surgery or replacement without package-level incompatibility evidence.
Stop when any code check reveals a release-path parse error, recurring runtime error, duplicate terminal transition, or upgrade transaction that can commit twice.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different strategy from prior tuning: repair authoritative owner handoffs and explicit contracts at the wave, release-shell/spatial, and dense-receipt boundaries. Treat diagnostic setup as isolated instrumentation, retain the authored environment, and make every acceptance black-box retestable while leaving native-renderer verdicts to the host.

code: Run the project’s bounded Godot/GDScript parse and static checks on all changed scripts and scenes, including DenseWaveProfile.self_audit and upgrade projection eligibility checks.

Exercise direct route, Bellkeeper terminal ownership, upgrade transaction debounce, and teardown/reset invariants through candidate-owned unit or scene checks without using diagnostic fixtures as ordinary evidence.
runtime: Tester starts a fresh run with ordinary movement and automatic combat, records state before and after each WaveDirector transition, confirms Waves 1–5, one Bellkeeper request, normal defeat, victory, Result, Retry, and clean new-run state.

Tester performs the sparse spatial replay from spawn through landmark and perimeter checkpoints, collecting runtime state, collision/alignment receipts, and shipped-camera screenshots at the same framing.

GameLoop Runtime rebinds the candidate-scoped MCP sidecar if available, then runs tester_dense_prepare -> tester_dense_advance -> tester_dense_reset serially for three isolated cycles and records renderer classification, sample availability, distributions, and reset isolation.
visual: Capture the upgrade draft at native and scaled viewport states with keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus; verify silhouettes/icons, compact truthful deltas, no placeholder CURRENT values, and no clipping or overlap.

Capture shipped gameplay views at spawn, landmark traversal, perimeter traversal, Wave 5, Bellkeeper telegraph/phase/defeat, Result, and Retry; verify authored cemetery composition, external depth, landmark collision agreement, readable escape lanes, and absence of disappearance or occlusion drift.

done_when: A fresh ordinary run advances Waves 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 contiguously under ordinary input, with composition changes, elite timing, live enemy caps, and no diagnostic jump counted.

The Bellkeeper is requested exactly once during the final wave, exposes both phases and readable attacks, can be defeated through normal automatic combat, and produces terminal victory without duplicate terminal transitions.

The spatial contract uses expand or larger traversable scale around the intact authored package, preserves external world or external depth, aligns the central building or landmark with collision, and records no disappearance or occlusion during ordinary movement or movement replay.

A movement replay reaches the landmark and every boundary or perimeter checkpoint without pass-through, spawn-outside-map, camera drift, or unstable visibility; native streets remain authoritative and no authored child meshes are duplicated or repositioned.
